_comment: Per-patch content assertions, checked by scripts/apply_air_patches.py. must_contain: strings that MUST appear in the patch text. must_not_contain: strings that MUST NOT appear anywhere. A subtlety worth stating because four entries got it backwards: these match the RAW patch text, so a line a patch removes appears as '-<old text>' and a line it adds as '+<new text>'. Asserting must_not_contain on the OLD form of a rewritten line is therefore impossible - it appears as the removal. To assert a rewrite happened, put BOTH forms in must_contain, the old with a leading '-' and the new with a leading '+'. must_not_contain is for genuinely absent text: a stale construct that must not reappear, such as a platform condition being reinstated.

0001-restartable-engine.patch.why: Split EngineMain::shutdown() into per-session teardown plus shutdownProcess(), so the engine can be left and re-entered in one process.

0002-restart-selftest.patch.why: Add -restartselftest: two EngineMain sessions back to back, exiting after script loading.

0003-restart-realsession.patch.why: Add -restartrealtest: two sessions running real frames, quitting via FTX::System->quit().

0004-sdl-include-path.patch.why: A.I.R.'s MSVC build asks for <SDL/SDL.h>, which cannot resolve against the vendored SDL2 because its headers are flat. These are the include DIRECTORIES that go with the corrected spelling in patch 0015: the SDL2 source include dir, and SDL's GENERATED include-config-<config>/SDL2 which holds the real SDL_config.h - listed first so it wins over the source dispatcher that falls back to SDL_config_minimal.h. target_include_directories, not include_directories, because the latter also reached SDL's own add_subdirectory and broke SDL_mslibc.c. Each call sits after its add_library, since CMake requires the target to exist first.

0005-stdcxxfs-guard.patch.why: Do not link stdc++fs under MSVC; it is a GCC/MinGW library and does not exist there.

0012-glew-as-target.patch.why: Give A.I.R.'s bundled GLEW its own CMake target instead of globbing it into rmxmedia, so a host linking its own GLEW has exactly one copy to link.

0006-endswith-data-call.patch.why: StringImpl.h passed str.data - a char* member - to includesAt, which takes a String. AIR's String has no such member, and its const char* is a call, not a field. Rewrite so it needs neither.

0007-adddouble-duplicate-decl.patch.why: addDouble was declared twice in String.h with different bodies. A TU that includes the header sees a duplicate declaration, which MSVC rejects.

0008-operator-assign-dependent-cast.patc.why: operator= on a template-dependent return type did `return *this;`, which needs a conversion to CLASS& that is only valid in a non-template context. Every implicit use was a compile error.
must_contain: +	CLASS& operator=(const StdString& str)		{ copy(str); return (CLASS&)*this; }

0011-remove-dead-getunicode.patch.why: getUnicode(size_t) and getUnicode(int) were declared and defined but never called and never instantiated by AIR. As written they do not compile - toUnicode is a member of StringTraits declared ~215 lines later, invisible to unqualified lookup at template-definition time - so any host TU that instantiated them failed on AIR's code rather than its own.
must_contain: +	// [Sonic Hybrid Ultimate] Removed getUnicode(size_t) and getUnicode(int).

0013-game-layer-as-library.patch.why: Compile Oxygen/sonic3air/source/sonic3air/*.cpp into a static library as well as the Sonic3AIR executable. That directory holds the only implementations of EngineDelegateInterface, GuiBase and AudioOutBase, and because they existed solely inside an executable there was nothing for a host to link against - a host embedding the engine had to reimplement the Sonic 3 front end by hand. main.cpp is excluded because it holds the tree's only main().

0014-honour-use-discord-on-windows.patch.why: Make USE_DISCORD gate Windows and Mac as well as Linux. The original condition enabled Discord on any non-GCC Windows build and on any Mac not defining NO_DISCORD, while A.I.R.'s CMake links discord_game_sdk_source only inside `if (USE_DISCORD)`. There was therefore no value of USE_DISCORD that made Windows agree with the link line, and USE_DISCORD=OFF gave 12 unresolved discord:: symbols. Upstream defect, not a misconfiguration.

0015-sdl-include-spelling.patch.why: The vendored SDL2 keeps its public headers flat - include/SDL.h and include/SDL_syswm.h exist, include/SDL/ and include/SDL2/ do not - so <SDL/SDL.h> and <SDL/SDL_syswm.h> can never resolve and no include path can fix that. SDL's own sources spell these flat and SDL's CMake exports the matching directories. Four attempts to fix only the path each failed; the fourth was informative because with the directories configured correctly the error was byte-for-byte identical. The GCC branch is untouched: it builds against an MSYS2 SDL2 laid out as SDL2/SDL.h.
